ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 3 — Sick Visit — Calamity Jane — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Same-day sick visit for a dental abscess

text.paragraph: Toothache for five days and a swollen jaw for two. [S]

Ms. Canary came in without an appointment because of a toothache in her lower left jaw for five days, with swelling of the jaw for two days and chills last night. The pain throbs, keeps her awake and is worse with hot or cold drinks. She can open her mouth fully and swallow, and has no swelling under the tongue or in the neck and no trouble breathing. She has no dentist and has not been able to afford one. She has taken naltrexone 50 mg daily for two weeks, though she missed two days while moving her things. She has not had a drink, though she said the pain made her think of whiskey, and a man in town offered her some of his prescription pain pills, which she turned down. She asked whether she could take something stronger for the pain. [S]

list.item:
Dental abscess of a lower left molar with fever (K04.7). An abscess at the root of a decayed molar, with facial swelling and fever but no spread to the floor of the mouth or neck. The decisive treatment is drainage or removal of the tooth; with fever and swelling an antibiotic is added, as the ADA guideline advises for systemic involvement. [S]
Amoxicillin 500 mg three times daily for five days.
The community health center's dental clinic will see her tomorrow morning for drainage or extraction; the clinic will cover the visit until her Medicaid is approved.
Ibuprofen 400 mg every 8 hours with food and acetaminophen 500 mg every 6 hours, no more than 2,000 mg a day.
Go to the emergency department at once for swelling under the tongue or in the neck, trouble swallowing or breathing, or trouble opening the mouth.

Severe alcohol use disorder on naltrexone (F10.20). No opioid was prescribed: naltrexone blocks opioids, and trying to overcome the block with high doses can cause a fatal overdose; the ibuprofen and acetaminophen combination works as well for dental pain. She was praised for turning down the pills and was reminded never to take opioids while on naltrexone. No alcohol. Safety reviewed: no thoughts of suicide or self-harm. [S]
Continue naltrexone 50 mg daily; a pill organizer given for the two missed days.
Peer recovery specialist to call her tomorrow.

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: The American Psychiatric Association Practice Guideline for the Pharmacological Treatment of Patients With Alcohol Use Disorder (2018); VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline for Assessment and Management of Patients at Risk for Suicide (2024); Evidence-based clinical practice guideline on antibiotic use for the urgent management of pulpal- and periapical-related dental pain and intraoral swelling (2019)

Follow-up: Dental clinic tomorrow morning. Phone check in two days. Four-week review in one week. Return at once as above. Next scheduled visit 1901-03-30: four-week review: naltrexone and the change to a monthly injection, liver stiffness, mood after four weeks without alcohol, and benefits. [S]
